data.narrative:
Fulfil is a Series B robotics and manufacturing company that has raised $127M to date. The valuation assessment relies on a comp universe of nine private companies and one public comparator across the robotics and manufacturing sector, with particular focus on three same-stage peers: Generalist AI ($2.0B), Bedrock Robotics ($1.8B), and Dexterity ($1.6B).

Two methods triangulate the valuation. Stage-progression analysis applies a 1.9x multiplier to the $127M total raised as a proxy base, yielding $241M. Peer-median analysis uses the three same-sector, same-stage comparables, which trade at a $1.6B–$2.0B range with a median of $1.8B. This wider range reflects heterogeneity in commercial traction and technology maturity within the cohort.

The two methods produce a wide triangulated range: $205M (low), $996M (median), and $2.0B (high). The stage-progression method anchors near the lower bound, while peer-median dominates the upper portion of the range. Key uncertainties include Fulfil's unit economics and customer concentration relative to the peer set, neither of which is available in the data. The dispersion between methods—spanning approximately 10x from low to high—suggests material sensitivity to assumptions about capital efficiency and market positioning within the robotics manufacturing vertical.
